comment: Nine two-particle runs at rest, T=4, dt 0.02, along x (requests 003-011, my review account). Fitted coefficients (1-D fit, P=2.5, mean of the two particles) against the paper's 0.86 (sep 7) and 0.65 (sep 9) law and the paper's model.py run unmodified out of sample. Sep 7: C-C 10.38 (pred 10.63, -2.4%); A-A 15.23 (15.48, -1.6%); B-B 5.11 (5.26, -2.9%); A-C K_A(C) -7.22 (-7.54, -4%), K_C(A) -17.39 (-18.28, -4.9%); B-C K_B(C) -5.28 (-5.25, +0.6%), K_C(B) -8.45 (-9.11, -7.3%); A-B K_A(B) 7.39 (7.73, -4.4%), K_B(A) 10.87 (10.61, +2.5%). Sep 9: C-C 7.95 (8.03, -1%); A-A 11.82 (11.70, +1%); A-B K_A(B) 5.66 (5.84, -3%), K_B(A) 8.08 (8.02, +0.7%). The paper's predictor reproduces all nine runs at tracker noise: rms 0.047-0.054 per coordinate, |mean residual| <= 0.008, max |residual| <= 0.20, no events. Not falsified: no coefficient misses the law by more than 7%, and the sep-9 factor holds to 1-3%. Narrowed for three reasons. (1) The single factor is not sharp: my sep-7 ratios K(7)/K(5) run from 0.80 to 0.88 across nine coefficients (mean about 0.84), so 0.86 sits at the top of the spread. K_C(B) misses its prediction by 7% in my run and 4.5% in the paper's own two runs, which the 6% tolerance in c6 does not cover cleanly. (2) Separation 8 lies inside the stated r_range [7,9], but model.py raises ValueError there and no run tests it. The claim should name the two separations 7 and 9 only; proposed_domain is written as [7,9] for that reason. (3) A-B is now tested at 7 and 9 and agrees within about 5%; the paper should either claim A-B or say it is untested. Scope of my runs: one run per pair at sep 7 and 9 (no repeats), so each coefficient carries about 3-4% run-to-run scatter.
